title: Western Yan
capsule: Western Yan was a short-lived Xianbei state of the Sixteen Kingdoms era, founded in 384 by Murong Hong of the Murong clan after the Former Qin's catastrophic defeat at the Battle of Fei River (383) triggered the fragmentation of Fu Jian's empire. The state cycled through seven rulers in barely a decade—virtually all through assassination or violent overthrow—reflecting factional chaos among the Murong aristocracy as the state migrated from the Chang'an area eastward into Shanxi, establishing its capital at Zhangzi in 386. Western Yan was destroyed in 394 when Murong Chui of the restored Later Yan invaded, defeating and killing the last ruler Murong Yong and reunifying the Murong Xianbei under a single authority.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Western Yan's territorial extent is imprecisely known; the state is not counted among the canonical Sixteen Kingdoms in Chinese dynastic historiography, and its boundaries must be inferred from scattered textual references rather than systematic geographic descriptions.
